inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero market: POT is an NZX filer with no material share-based payment (small employee share scheme only, <NZ$1m). SBC rows kept explicit at 0% per house rule; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.share_count_basis: 680.909m ordinary shares, flat for a decade; no buyback programme (the ~NZ$0.6-0.8m/yr 'repurchases' are employee-scheme housekeeping), no dilution
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-08-26 NZX close 8.115 (verified market data supplied by orchestrator; regular close, not volatile)
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (operating company), 10-year component build, per dcf-methods routing -- POT is a capital-intensive monopoly port operator, not a REIT/bank/LIC. Section 7 adaptations applied: (1) NZD WACC 7.75% built from NZ 10yr govt ~4.4% + 5.0% ERP at beta ~0.75, ~10% debt weight at ~3.8% after-tax -- NO small-cap illiquidity premium (NZX-50 large cap, A-/Stable, monopoly asset). (2) Leases treatment A: NZ$58.7m lease liabilities included in net debt, lease principal (~NZ$1m/yr, immaterial) NOT deducted from flows. (3) No NCI. (4) Matching-asset rule: share of profit from equity-accounted investees (FY2025 NZ$6.2m -- Northport Group NGL, Coda, PrimePort) is EXCLUDED from the flows (core EBITDA = revenue - opex = 228.4 in FY2025, 49.2% margin, vs reported EBITDA 234.5 which includes the EAI share), and the matching assets (investments NZ$284.1m + advances NZ$38.1m = NZ$322.2m at Dec-2025 carrying value, NGL marked to fair value Jun-2025) are added in the bridge. This also avoids extrapolating a historical associate line whose composition changed with the FY2025 Northport disposal. (5) Risk charged once: Stella Passage consent risk lives in the scenario weights (bear 25%), WACC is a clean single rate across scenarios. FY2025 BASE-YEAR ADJUSTMENTS: reported NPAT 173.4 includes the one-off NZ$49.245m gain on disposal of equity-accounted investees -- underlying NPAT 126.0 used throughout; reported FY2025 FCF 143.8 is flattered by consent-blocked Stella Passage capex (28.1 vs ~NZ$40-45m mid-cycle) -- last_fcf 127.0 = OCF 172.0 less normalized capex 45.0. Interest income (NZ$0.7m) immaterial and POT is a net-debt company -- no strip. CAPEX SUPERCYCLE modelled explicitly: base case consent granted FY2027, capex steps up 90/140/140/100/70 over FY2027-31 before settling at 8.5% of revenue.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blended revenue path: FY2026 +8% (guidance-anchored, H1 +8.5% actual), decelerating to 2.5% by year 10; 10yr revenue CAGR is 7.3%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: equity_5yr_cagr 13.7% diverges >30% from revenue (9.0%) and underlying-EPS (7.3%) CAGRs -- driven by the FY2022 port-land revaluation (equity jumped 1,397 to 2,074), not retained earnings; equity CAGR rejected as the growth anchor. EPS CAGRs computed on UNDERLYING NPAT (kpis.UnderlyingNetProfit), stripping the FY2025 NZ$49.2m disposal gain. FCF CAGRs are capex-timing noise (consent-blocked capex trough in FY2025) -- not used.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is zero for this NZX filer, so owner-FCF and reported-FCF series coincide; the FCF CAGR distortion here is capex phasing, not SBC.

scenario_narratives.base: Stella Passage fast-track consent granted during FY2027 (re-lodged Jan-2026 under the amended Act); berth extension + automated cranes built FY2027-2031 with capex peaking ~NZ$140m/yr, suppressing FCF mid-decade before capacity lifts volumes. Revenue +8% FY2026 (guidance: underlying NPAT 142-152) decelerating to 2.5%; core EBITDA margin recovers 49.2% to 52% on crane/ship-rate productivity, MetroPort repricing and tariff increases. Terminal growth 2.25% (NZ long-run nominal GDP).
scenario_narratives.bull: Consent clears cleanly and early; container volumes push past the FY2022 peak (1.24m TEU) as bigger ships consolidate calls at the only NZ port that can berth them; Ruakura/Rolleston inland hubs scale and MetroPort economics improve further; margin reaches 53.5%. Faster, larger build (capex peaks NZ$150m). Terminal growth 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Consent blocked again by fresh judicial review or iwi negotiation impasse -- Stella Passage shelved for the decade; NZ export-commodity cycle stays soft (weak China log demand, dairy/kiwifruit seasonality) and alliance restructuring trims Tauranga call frequency; margin stalls ~49%; capex is maintenance-only (~9%/rev) so near-term FCF actually exceeds base, but there is no capacity-driven growth and terminal value is materially lower. Terminal growth 2.0%.

entry_price.note: TV at exit is the scenario's WACC-based Gordon value (fair price a buyer pays in FY2035); only the discounting to today uses the 15% hurdle. A 15% NZD IRR on a ~7.75%-WACC monopoly infrastructure asset requires an entry near NZ$2.31 -- less than a third of today's price; the hurdle is essentially unattainable in this name.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_N)), so the flows and the exit are charged the same rate. Corrected 2026-09-01.

sensitivity.note: Full model rebuilt at each (WACC, g) pair; 20x terminal cap binds in the low-WACC/high-g corners (the flat cells).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25% because the Stella Passage consent has ALREADY been struck down once (High Court, Aug-2025) and iwi/hapu cultural-impact objections remain unresolved -- a repeat blockage is a live, demonstrated path. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs three things to go right at once: fast consent, volume recovery past the FY2022 peak, and margin expansion to 53.5%. Consent risk is charged HERE, not in the WACC (risk charged once).
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide, the accounting-regime band collapses to a point, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0%.

historical_multiples_10yr.basis: FY-end (June) closing prices supplied by orchestrator x 680.909m shares; underlying NPAT for FY2021-25 (kpis.UnderlyingNetProfit), reported NPAT before; company net-debt convention (borrowings - cash); CSV FY EBITDA (includes EAI share). P/E and EV/EBITDA are SBC-unadjusted AND SBC-adjusted simultaneously -- SBC is zero for POT, so the two bases coincide by identity.

sanity_check.trip_direction: conservative -- IV implies multiples below POT's own historical trading floor, not above its ceiling
sanity_check.diagnosis: Auto-diagnosis found no component error: the base year is mid-cycled correctly (underlying NPAT 126.0 not reported 173.4; capex normalized), the margin path is anchored to actuals, tax is statutory 28%, WACC 7.75% is at the LOW end of the sanctioned 7.5-9.0% range with no illiquidity premium, and risk is charged once. The gap is a market-pricing phenomenon, not a modelling one: POT has traded at 31-59x earnings and 18-35x EV/EBITDA for a decade because it is an irreplaceable monopoly with a 54% council holder restricting float and index/income demand concentrated in the free float -- a documented scarcity premium, the same finding as AIA.NZ (house IV $1.90 vs $8.76). At NZ$8.115 the market accepts a ~5.5-6% forward IRR; any defensible NZD discount rate in 7.5-9.0% produces an IV far below the price. Cross-check: Jarden NZ$7.00 (underweight) sits near the market-multiple reference below; Forsyth Barr NZ$9.40 (neutral, 'relatively expensive') assumes current multiples persist.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Per 8c.4/8c.5, no forced change to the house IV (the trip is conservative-direction and diagnosable). Two disciplines applied instead: (1) a supplementary MARKET-MULTIPLE REFERENCE VALUE published below -- exit at POT's own 10yr median EV/EBITDA of 22.8x on Y10 core EBITDA gives NZ$7.17/share, so the gap house 4.14 -> reference 7.17 -> price 8.12 prices the scarcity-premium re-rate assumption explicitly instead of burying it in a terminal assumption; (2) the house Gordon TV's implied exit EV/EBITDA (11.2x base) is disclosed per scenario so the reader can see the house model assumes roughly HALF POT's historical trading multiple at exit.

market_multiple_reference.note: Reference value = base-case explicit FCF + terminal at the 10yr median trading multiple, all at 7.75% WACC. It answers 'what if the market keeps paying what it has always paid' -- a re-rate-persists memo, NOT the house basis.

sanity_check.note: Multiples computed on POT's own history per instruction (monopoly + council float restriction make generic industrial benchmarks inapplicable). Adjusted and unadjusted multiples coincide because SBC is zero.

valuation_philosophy: Port of Tauranga is the highest-quality infrastructure asset on the NZX -- a genuine monopoly with the only berths in New Zealand able to take the largest container ships, an A-/Stable balance sheet at 17% gearing, and a demonstrated ability to reprice (MetroPort) and to sweat assets (crane rate +3.5%, ship rate +12.7%). The valuation problem is not the business, it is the price of the business. On component-built owner FCF -- underlying NPAT of ~NZ$147m guided for FY2026, a Stella Passage capex supercycle that will absorb most free cash flow for FY2027-31, and a 52% mature core EBITDA margin -- the equity is worth ~NZ$4.14/share at a 7.75% NZD WACC, and even the bull case (NZ$4.89) sits 40% below the NZ$8.12 market price. The market instead prices POT at 37x underlying earnings and 22x EV/EBITDA, a ~5.5-6% forward IRR, because the 54% Bay of Plenty Regional Council stake restricts float and income/passive demand is captive -- the same scarcity premium documented on AIA.NZ. Holding POT's own decade-median exit multiple (the market-multiple reference) gets to NZ$7.17, almost exactly Jarden's NZ$7.00 underweight target; today's NZ$8.12, at the very top of the decade range, additionally requires that premium to widen. This is an income-and-modest-growth name (~85% payout, ~2.2% yield) whose current price embeds bond-like required returns plus a successful, on-time Stella Passage build; it offers no margin of safety against either the discount rate normalising or the consent stalling again.

reasonableness_cross_check.note: Cross-check only, not an input. House base 4.14 is below both because sell-side targets capitalize at prevailing market multiples; the market-multiple reference value 7.17 reconciles almost exactly to Jarden.
